Let the tetrahedron have vertices \(P\) (top), \(A\) (front), and \(B,C\) (the two lower base vertices). The cut plane is the shaded triangle through \(B,C\) and the midpoint \(M\) of edge \(PA\).

The plane divides the tetrahedron into two pieces sharing the same triangular base \(BCM\):

- one piece with apex \(A\),
- one piece with apex \(P\).

Since \(M\) is the midpoint of \(PA\), points \(A\) and \(P\) are at equal perpendicular distances from the cutting plane through \(BCM\). Thus the two tetrahedra have equal volumes.

So the part containing \(A\) has volume
\[
\frac{216}{2}=108.
\]

\]
